leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor of Higher Education (and Acting Chancellor, 1977)
leaders.priorInstitution: New Jersey Department of Higher Education
leaders.notes: Sixth president and by far the longest-serving in campus history at 34 years; in office throughout 1996, so his true 1979 start is recorded here. Earlier he was associate vice chancellor for academic affairs at the University of Kansas. The campus dedicated James M. Rosser Hall in his honor in 2017.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Seventh president; external to the campus but internal to the CSU system, arriving from the Fresno provostship (and earlier the Stanislaus State provostship). Announced his retirement in August 2022, effective June 30, 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: President Emeritus (retired from the presidency in 2020)
leaders.notes: Appointed interim president by CSU Interim Chancellor Jolene Koester; served July 31, 2023 to January 7, 2024. A 40-year CSU veteran who led Cal State East Bay 2011-2020 and spent 30 years at San Francisco State before that.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.priorInstitution: York College, City University of New York
leaders.notes: Ninth president and the first woman to lead Cal State LA; took office January 8, 2024. External hire from CUNY, though she had earlier been vice president for student affairs at Cal State Fullerton (2012-2019). No active presidential search found.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Retired; remained active on campus and in the community until his death on December 6, 2021
leaders.notes: Longest-serving Sacramento State president (19 years); in office throughout 1996, so his true 1984 start is recorded. Came from the Dominguez Hills presidency (1976-1984), so a CSU-internal but campus-external move. Later wrote a history of the CSU system.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Led Sacramento State for 12 years after six years as president of CSU San Marcos; earlier spent 18 years at Fresno State as faculty member, department chair and provost. Another CSU-internal, campus-external move.

leaders.priorTitle: Special Advisor to the Executive Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Eighth permanent president, appointed March 2015 and took office July 1, 2015. Immediately prior he advised the UT System after serving as president of the University of Texas-Pan American (2010-2014). Announced his retirement November 2, 2022; last day July 1, 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Student Affairs and Campus Diversity and Chief Diversity Officer
leaders.notes: Ninth permanent president, took office July 16, 2023. A Sacramento State alumnus (BA in Black History and Politics, MA in Higher Education Leadership) and a former foster child; at SDSU he was the first Black Distinguished Professor in that institution's history. No active presidential search found.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, College of Business Administration
leaders.nextRole: Retired; Campus Ambassador Emeritus. Died January 22, 2008
leaders.notes: Eleventh president; a fully internal promotion after 20 years at CMU as business professor, assistant dean and then dean of the College of Business Administration (1979-92). Named interim president in 1992 and permanent president in 1994; retired July 31, 2000. In office throughout 1996.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor
leaders.notes: Twelfth president. Began his higher education career as president of Mission College in California, then chancellor of Montana State University-Northern (1998-2000) before CMU. Left in 2009 to become the fifth president of Virginia Commonwealth University and VCU Health System.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Government Relations and Public Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Returned to her post as Vice President for Government Relations and Public Affairs; named Vice President for Development and External Affairs in 2011
leaders.notes: Thirteenth president and the first woman to lead CMU, serving on an interim basis after Rao's departure. Joined CMU in 2002 after a career in Michigan state government, where she was the first woman to direct three state departments. Died in 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: Fourteenth president, serving March 1, 2010 to July 31, 2018. Returned to CMU from the Alcorn State presidency, having previously been CMU's vice president for finance and administrative services, so an external appointment with prior campus ties.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: President Emeritus and University Professor (full professor), starting faculty duties spring 2026
leaders.notes: Fifteenth president, appointed September 1, 2018. Had earlier been president of Eastern Oregon University before Murray State. Announced in January 2024 that he would step down effective December 31, 2024, citing personal and professional reasons; his successor took office November 1, 2024, so no interim was needed.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Sixteenth president, appointed unanimously by the Board of Trustees in September 2024 and took office November 1, 2024. A pharmacist by training with 26 years in higher education; formally invested in April 2025. No active presidential search found.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor
leaders.nextRole: Vice President and Director, Office of Women in Higher Education (later Vice President for the Effective Leadership Program)
leaders.notes: Fourth president and the first woman to lead Cleveland State, taking office April 20, 1993; in office throughout 1996. Oversaw the conversion to the semester system in 1998. Died September 29, 2021 at age 86 of injuries from a car crash in Needham, Massachusetts.

leaders.priorTitle: President Emeritus and Trustees Professor
leaders.nextRole: Retired; President Emeritus. Died in January 2024
leaders.notes: Fifth president. Served roughly one year as interim president beginning in 2001 before being appointed president and installed September 26, 2002; the official past-presidents list therefore dates his term 2002-2009. Previously president of Kent State University (1982-1991). Built enrollment standards, an honors program, and major new buildings including the Student Center and Recreation Center.

Sixth president, 2009-2018, per the university's official past-presidents list. His immediately preceding position and his post-presidency role could not be confirmed from official or press sources within this research pass and are deliberately left blank.

Seventh president. Departed April 26, 2022 after four years in what the Board of Trustees called a mutually agreed-upon separation over differences about the university's future direction; he was not fired and no single triggering event was cited. His package included roughly $928,000 and the option of a tenured professorship at the Cleveland-Marshall College of Law, though it is unconfirmed whether he took it. Prior position not verified.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Eighth president, appointed April 26, 2022 and promoted straight from the provostship with no interim designation and no national search. She had joined Cleveland State in fall 2021 from the University of Minnesota, where she was dean of the Humphrey School of Public Affairs. Was a finalist for the University of Minnesota presidency in February 2024 but was passed over and stated she has no intention of seeking another presidency. No active presidential search found.

university: The City College of New York

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs and Professor of Anthropology
leaders.notes: Tenth president and the first woman to lead City College; in office throughout 1996, so her true 1993 start is recorded. Left July 2, 1999 under pressure from CUNY trustees during the fight over remediation and admissions policy. Later became associate vice chancellor at UC Riverside.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Sophie Davis School of Biomedical Education
leaders.priorInstitution: The City College of New York (same campus)
leaders.nextRole: Returned as Dean of the Sophie Davis School of Biomedical Education until his retirement in 2009
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: The City College of New York
leaders.notes: Served as interim president between Moses's forced departure in 1999 and Gregory Williams's arrival in 2001, charged with redirecting the campus after the CUNY remediation fight. A fully internal appointment.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the Michael E. Moritz College of Law and Carter C. Kissell Professor of Law
leaders.notes: Eleventh president, taking office August 2001. Enrollment grew roughly 60 percent to more than 16,000; he opened The Towers residence hall, completed the Spitzer School of Architecture, and led a first capital campaign raising over $310 million. Resigned effective November 1, 2009 to become the 27th president of the University of Cincinnati. Author of the memoir 'Life on the Color Line'; died August 12, 2025.

leaders.priorTitle: Distinguished Professor of Civil Engineering and Director, University Transportation Research Center
leaders.priorInstitution: The City College of New York (same campus)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to the faculty as Distinguished Professor of Civil Engineering
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: The City College of New York
leaders.notes: Served as interim president from October 15, 2009 to August 2, 2010, bridging Williams's departure and Coico's arrival. A fully internal appointment; a nationally known transportation scholar who later received CCNY's President's Medal.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Twelfth president and a CCNY alumna, published at Temple under the name Lisa Staiano-Coico. Resigned abruptly in October 2016 while she and an affiliated nonprofit foundation were under federal investigation over her personal expenses and the handling of research funds. Her post-resignation role could not be verified.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Colin Powell School for Civic and Global Leadership
leaders.priorInstitution: The City College of New York (same campus)
leaders.notes: Named interim president effective November 2, 2016 by CUNY Chancellor James B. Milliken after Coico's resignation, then appointed permanent president by the CUNY Board of Trustees on December 4, 2017; the single entry covers the continuous tenure. A fully internal appointment: founding director (2002-13) and founding dean (2013-16) of the Colin Powell School and a professor of political science specializing in Southeast Asian social movements. No active presidential search found.
